summary: git commit --amend replaces the most recent commit. Use it to fix the message or add a file you forgot.
notes: Amend makes a new commit with a new hash. The old one is no longer on the branch.
--no-edit keeps the existing message. -m sets a new one.
To change an older commit, make a new commit that fixes it, or use git revert.
pitfall: Amending a commit you already pushed makes git push fail with "rejected (non-fast-forward)". Only amend commits that are still local.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with one commit that has gradebook.py, README.md, and scores.csv.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
